headline: Sudan army drone strikes kill 300+ in West Kordofan and Abyei
dek: Sudanese army drone strikes killed 300+: ~150 in West Kordofan (Oct 18, incl. 145 in truck of ~200 mourners at Al-Dabab + 5 in funeral tent, per Sudan War Observatory) and 153 at Amiet/Al-Na'am market in disputed Abyei (Oct 19, per Abyei info minister).
sources: BBC (via Sudan War Observatory + Abyei info minister Yohana Akol Ngor to AP/Reuters); Sudan military source to BBC
fault_line: Was this a legitimate RSF-supply strike or a mass killing of civilians — and will South Sudan be dragged into Sudan's war?

sections.what_happened: Sudanese army drone strikes killed 300+: ~150 in West Kordofan (Oct 18, incl. 145 in truck of ~200 mourners at Al-Dabab + 5 in funeral tent, per Sudan War Observatory) and 153 at Amiet/Al-Na'am market in disputed Abyei (Oct 19, per Abyei info minister). Military source confirmed army carried out Abyei strike, claiming RSF fuel-supply target; MSF received 20+ burn/shrapnel patients; South Sudan summoned Sudan's ambassador in protest.
sections.what_verified: BBC reporting; AP/Reuters carried Akol Ngor 153 figure; multiple independent relays; army source confirmed attack; UN's Dujarric alarmed by strikes
sections.what_disputed: Tolls are reported, not independently counted; army officer claims dead were RSF/fuel smugglers ('we do not target civilians'); Al-Mujlad market casualty figures unverified; no independent satellite/ground verification beyond BBC Verify satellite images of burnt Amiet market
sections.why_matters: One of the deadliest single bursts of Sudan's war — 300+ dead in two days — while the world watches Ukraine/Gaza; army source itself confirmed the Abyei strike
sections.context: Background: Sudan — NEW MISSED ITEM: Sudan army drone strikes kill 300+ in West Kordofan and Abyei (Oct 18-19)

totw_analysis: Our read: One of the deadliest single bursts of Sudan's war — 300+ dead in two days — while the world watches Ukraine/Gaza; army source itself confirmed the Abyei strike The fault line our audience is arguing over: Was this a legitimate RSF-supply strike or a mass killing of civilians — and will South Sudan be dragged into Sudan's war?
